subject: Temporary log-retention addendum & backup purge hold — Healthera
messages:
From: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@healthera.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@healthera.com
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary log-retention for regulatory review / DPA addendum

Hi Jordan,

We have an incoming regulatory inquiry in the UK that may require us to preserve certain access and audit logs for a longer period than our standard contract with Redwood currently allows. Our legal team has asked whether Redwood can: 

- Pause backup purge for the affected tenant for 90 days (starting immediately)
- Provide an addendum or short DPA amendment that documents the temporary retention carve-out and audit access commitments
- Supply SOC2 evidence and a notarized log-handling statement for the period of the hold

I've attached a short request from Healthera legal (healthera_legal_request_20260601.pdf) and a redline showing suggested language.

Can you confirm whether a temporary hold is possible and what the timeline / approvals process would look like? We need to coordinate with procurement and our security team for signatures.

Thanks,
Sarah Mills
Head of Legal Operations
Healthera

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary log-retention for regulatory review / DPA addendum

Hi Sarah — thanks for the detailed note and the legal request. 

Short answer: yes, we can support a temporary suspension of backup purge for a scoped tenant while the regulatory review is ongoing, but we need to coordinate legal redlines, a formal DPA amendment, and an operational runbook. To set expectations: 

- Approval path: Legal (Redwood) + Security + Ops sign-off, then DocuSign with Healthera.
- Timeline: We can implement a pause on the next maintenance window (within 48 hours of signed amendment) and provide an operations runbook for access to preserved logs.
- Evidence: We can produce SOC2 summary reports and a signed operational attestation; full SOC2 reports require your NDA/procurement flow.

I've attached a proposed retention schedule and an initial proposed clause that legal can redline (rw-retention-proposal-20260602.xlsx).

Action items I propose: 
1) Kimberly, can you review the attached redline from Healthera and the clause in the workbook and suggest DPA language we can present?
2) Marissa / Ops: estimate effort and confirm whether a scoped pause (by tenant id) is feasible without taking the tenant offline.
3) Sarah / Healthera: confirm which data classes and log types must be preserved (application logs, access logs, KV snapshots, backups) and confirm the requested hold start date.

If that plan works, we'll prep a short amendment and a one-page runbook for your security team to review.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: temporary log-retention for regulatory review / DPA addendum

Jordan — appreciate the quick turnaround. Healthera confirms the scope: 

- Data classes: access logs (auth/iam), API request logs, audit trails tied to patient records, and encrypted snapshot metadata. No raw customer content.
- Requested hold: 90 calendar days, starting 2026-06-02 (we understand the window above, so the effective start can be the next maintenance window once the amendment is signed).
- Evidence: we need a SOC2 summary and the attestation letter; if possible, a screenshot of the log retention policy applied to our tenant after enforcement.

Attached is our redline (redline_healthera_dpa_v1.docx) that clarifies retention window and preservation scope. We can accept a single-page DPA amendment (Annex) with references to the underlying DPA and this temporary carve-out.

Questions from our procurement team: will this hold incur additional fees? If so, what cadence (one-time or monthly)?

Thanks — Sarah

Subject: Re: Request: temporary log-retention for regulatory review / DPA addendum

Sarah / Jordan — looped in Legal and Ops notes below and attached a drafting proposal.

On the legal side: we can issue a short-form DPA amendment ("Annex G — Temporary Retention Addendum") that references the master DPA and specifies: 
- Scope by tenant ID (we will include the Healthera tenant GUID in the Annex)
- Types of records to preserve: auth logs, API request logs, audit trails, snapshot metadata
- Effective period: 90 days from the effective date (the Annex will state an effective date = date of last signature)
- Access controls: read-only access for Healthera security and authorized Redwood ops during the hold; Redwood will not use the preserved logs for training or other product uses.
- Fees: a one-time administrative fee to cover extended storage and legal amendment (~USD 3,500) and a nominal monthly storage surcharge if the hold exceeds 90 days (we propose USD 500/month after day 90).

Operational notes from Ops (Marissa): 
- We can implement tenant-scoped pause of automatic backup purge without downtime; ETA for enactment is within 48 hours of signed Annex.
- We'll provide an operations runbook and a screenshot of the retention policy applied to the tenant (as requested).
- Attachments: suggested Annex text and a checklist for control evidence.

Next steps: 
1) Jordan: please confirm acceptance of the fee profile with Healthera procurement.
2) Sarah: if Healthera accepts, we'll circulate the Annex for signature via DocuSign (link below).
3) Marissa / Ops: once signed, Ops will lock purge jobs for the tenant and deliver the screenshot and attestation within 24 hours.

DocuSign draft: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/SAMPLE-ENVELOPE-ID
Drive folder with draft Annex & evidence checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cHealtheraDPA
